blockers.title: Fractional per-terminal cap (0.2 pkts/tick) is unenforceable as a per-tick integer comparison — the specified When-clause would skip EVERY residential spawn
blockers.evidence: stories-v2.md: 'When a spec's volume would assign more spawns to one terminal than its cap this tick' · core/flow.odin:645: 'for k in 0..<vol {' — integer per-tick spawn loop; cap proposed '~0.2 pkts/tick'
blockers.detail: Spawns are integer per tick (flow.odin `for k in 0..<vol`); a per-tick compare against 0.2 rejects every single spawn (1 > 0.2), so residential-sourced email never lands. No accumulator/token-bucket semantics or its run-state home is specified; the (20÷cap) formula only coheres with rate semantics.
blockers.recommended_fix: Specify the enforcement mechanism in Thread 2 + card 5.9: a per-terminal spawn accumulator (credit rate = cap, spawn costs 1; state home + T1 hash + determinism implications stated), or an integer form (1 spawn per N ticks).

blockers.title: Proposed cap (0.2 pkts/tick ≈ 6 u/s) exceeds residential throughput (5 u/s = 0.167 pkts/tick) and the pre-5.10 narrow service rate — 'endpoints never self-congest' fails at the spec's own starting values within card 5.9
blockers.evidence: spec §1: 'a single residential (throughput 5 u/s = 0.167 packets/tick) can be asked to source 4/tick, and packets drop at its own spawn (pool E22) and its own serialization (queue E9)' · Thread 2: 'Proposed starting point: ~0.2 pkts/tick for a residential ≈ 6 u/s demand vs the ~8–10 u/s access link' · node_types.json: residential throughput_units 5 · spec's own rule: content_host 'caps against ITS throughput ~2.67 pkts/tick' (=80/30, exactly its throughput)
blockers.detail: 5.9 lands before 5.10's narrow resize, so at 5.9 the access serves 5 u/tick (0.167 pkts/tick) < capped 0.2 → backlog → E9 sheds at the endpoint's own access lane, falsifying 5.9's launchable ('no residential is ever the drop site'). Also inconsistent with the spec's own per-type principle (content_host caps AT its throughput; residential caps 1.2× above it).
blockers.recommended_fix: Set the residential cap ≤ node throughput (≤0.167) with the access-resize headroom computed from that, or make 5.9+5.10 one landing unit; apply the caps-against-throughput rule uniformly.
